reason: The text explicitly demonstrates collaboration between King Josiah (the leader) and the people. The king gathers 'all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem' and directs them to the temple. Most significantly, the passage states that 'all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem' went to the temple with the king, priests, and prophets. The people then collectively participate in renewing the covenant: 'all the people stood in the covenant' (וַיַּעֲמֹד כָּל־ הָעָם בַּבְּרִית). Furthermore, when the king commands the people to celebrate Passover 'according to what is written in this Book of the Covenant,' they participate together in this religious observance. The narrative demonstrates a unified effort in which the leadership (king and priests) initiates reforms while the people actively participate and confirm their commitment through covenant renewal.
